key_insight: Learned smoothers improve fixed-budget multigrid accuracy for high-contrast elliptic problems, but the tested CPU implementation provides no computational advantage over classical solvers.
engineering_relevance: For finite-element simulation, better error reduction per cycle does not necessarily translate into faster solves.
method: Train only the smoothers within an operator-adapted multigrid V-cycle.
Use operator-dependent transfers, Galerkin coarse operators, near-kernel deflation and an energy-norm safeguard.
Compare energy errors against classical smoothing at fixed and increased iteration budgets.
evidence_signal: On fresh problems, one learned pass reduced energy error by factors of 5.7–6.1 on conductive channels and 1.38–1.45 on insulating barriers relative to the same cycle with four-step Jacobi-preconditioned conjugate-gradient smoothing.
watch_item: Increasing classical smoothing erased the accuracy advantage, while load changes and floating islands further limited learned-cycle accuracy.
paper_title: Learned smoothing in operator-adapted multigrid: controlled accuracy gains and computational limits
